description: It's me guys, Winn. Now, let's win this!
summary: Tandem is a web app that helps astronauts check their own health on long missions, when a doctor may be minutes or months away. A two-minute morning check-in gathers vitals, blood sugar, food and water, sleep, exercise, mood and symptoms. Tandem turns these into five body-system scores, explains every flag in plain language, and gives one clear action with a checklist and a report to the flight surgeon. It also links the cabin’s microbes to the crew’s immune score, modelled on NASA’s ISS microbiome study, and flags when how an astronaut feels and what their signals show don’t match. It matters because on long missions astronauts must spot health changes in themselves.
details:
What it does: Tandem gathers health indicators, evaluates them and tells the astronaut what to do. Features include a morning check-in, five system scores with reasons, action checklists, a health log, per-module cabin microbe swabs, a crewmate check, a tappable body map, 14-day trend charts, “how to measure” guides, check-in streaks, three mission profiles (ISS, Moon, Mars) with signal delay, and day and night modes.

How it works: simple, explainable rules. Heart rate and heart rate variability are compared with the astronaut’s own early-mission normal; other readings are checked against safe ranges. The overall status follows the worst system, so one serious problem is never averaged away.

Benefits: it runs offline on any device, takes two minutes a day, and explains itself. The same approach fits polar stations, ships, offshore platforms and other remote crews.

Tools: HTML, CSS and JavaScript in one self-contained file, with no backend. GitHub, Vercel, Playwright and axe-core for testing.

Limitations: crew data is simulated, thresholds are demonstration values, and Tandem is a prototype, not a medical device.

Source code: https://github.com/winnn25/tandem
